articles.title: Alan Greenspan, influential Fed chair who shaped modern US capitalism, dies at 100

articles.summary: Tribals in Bastar have revived protests against the proposed Bodhghat dam as fresh surveys begin. Thousands from 56 villages gathered, saying the project will displace communities and submerge sacred forests, hills and cultural sites. While the government says the dam will boost irrigation and development, locals see it as a threat to their land, identity and survival.

articles.title: June 2026: Mining Destabilizing Himalayan Rivers, Infrastructures in HP, UKD
articles.summary: A bridge on Malan river in Pauri district collapsed on July 12, 2023, amid flood surge in the river. Damage to the 300 m long bridge connecting Pauri with Kotdwar affected about 50,000 people. Locals and activists believed that the collapse was due to rampant illegal mining that had weakened the riverbed. They also reported that the riverbed mining started within 72 hours of bridge collapse. The locals were constantly reporting about illegal mining and sinking of their houses and farm land.

articles.title: China hits back at US sanctions on tech giants, restricting its exports to 10 American defense firms
articles.summary: China has imposed restrictions on exporting 'dual-use' items to 10 American military-linked companies in response to US sanctions. This move is part of a broader trade dispute between China and the US. The impact of this decision is not clear, but it may have implications for global trade and security.
articles.raw_summary: China has retaliated against US sanctions by imposing its own restrictions on 10 American military-linked companies. Beijing's Commerce Ministry announced a ban on exporting "dual-use" items to these firms, citing national security and US "wrongful expansion" of its own blacklist. Additionally, Chinese government entities are now prohibited from purchasing products from 46 US companies, including major defense contractors.

articles.title: Meet Kunal Shah, serial entrepreneur and Meta's pick to lead WhatsApp
articles.summary: Indian tech entrepreneur Kunal Shah is set to lead WhatsApp, the world's largest messaging platform, succeeding Will Cathcart. Shah, the founder of fintech unicorn CRED and pioneer of digital payments with FreeCharge, brings extensive experience in building successful tech ventures. Meta's investment in CRED and Shah's deep understanding of user needs in India, WhatsApp's largest market, underscore the significance of this appointment for the global messaging giant's future strategy.
